answer: In a reputation-based Sybil resistance mechanism, agents assign reputation scores based on peer feedback. An attacker creating hollow identities would struggle to maintain a consistent signal across the network. As they create new identities, they must invest in establishing a reputation ridge, making it costly to fake multiple identities. An attacker would need to expend resources proportional to the number of fake identities, limiting the economic viability of large-scale Sybil attacks.
